body: Instead of using the video, why don't you just research for me how to stop a Stamina inversion table from going forward? If you give me a minute, I will get you the model.

Researched. The Stamina manual is blunt about it: "a very sensitive balance device. It responds to very slight changes in weight distribution." There is no forward stop — nothing mechanical prevents it tipping forward. It's all balance, and the manual's fix is the height adjustment plus their balance test:

1. Shorten the height setting on the boom — forward lunging means it's set too tall for her. The manual's test: lock in, lie back with hands at your sides. If your feet end up higher than your head, go taller; if it won't rotate near level, go shorter. It should return to upright on its own with hands at sides.
2. Check the pivot arms — there are three holes, and the manual says use the lowest ones until familiar. Lowest hole = least inversion angle.

So: drop the boom a notch or two, run the balance test, and confirm it sits still with her just standing on it.
